title: Exact sequences and short exact sequences in an abelian category
statement: Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian]. A sequence of morphisms $\cdots\to x_{i-1}\xrightarrow{d_{i-1}}x_i\xrightarrow{d_i}x_{i+1}\to\cdots$ of $\mathcal A$ (finite, $x_1\to\cdots\to x_n$, or infinite in one or both directions) is a *complex* if $d_i\circ d_{i-1}=0$ for every two consecutive arrows; a complex is *exact at* an object $x_i$ that has an arrow in and an arrow out if $\mathrm{Im}(d_{i-1})=\mathrm{Ker}(d_i)$ as subobjects of $x_i$, and it is *exact* if it is exact at every such object. A *short exact sequence* is an exact complex $0\to A\xrightarrow{f}B\xrightarrow{g}C\to0$; equivalently $g\circ f=0$, $f$ is a monomorphism, $g$ is an epimorphism and $\mathrm{Im}(f)=\mathrm{Ker}(g)$.
